COURSE OUTLINE2025/2026
COURSE NAME: Logic and Problem-Solving
COURSE CODE: SDEV1000
COURSE DESCRIPTION
Logic and problem-solving are crucial competencies for software developers as they underpin the creation of efficient and
functional code. This course will teach students logical steps and reasoning in problem-solving, critical thinking, flowcharting, and
mathematical concepts and ideas which enable students to create robust and scalable software applications.
Course Credits: 3.00
LEARNING OUTCOMES
OUTCOME Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to
1 Identify and apply basic principles of logical thinking and problem-solving for simple scenarios.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Explain algorithmic thinking and strategies•
Apply basic logic concepts, including conditionals and loops•
Develop problem-solving strategies using simple scenarios•
Analyze structured approaches to problem analysis and requirement gathering•
2 Create and interpret flowcharts to visualize problem-solving processes.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Use flowchart symbols to create a document•
chunks.label: Page 1

chunks.text:
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Use flowchart symbols to create a document•
Analyze requirements before creating flowcharts•
Create and interpret flowcharts to visualize problem-solving processes•
Convert flowcharts into pseudo-code•
Develop solutions using logical thinking and structures•
3 Analyze, develop, and validate solutions for progressively complex logical problems.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Apply mathematical concepts and calculations related to programming processes•
Analyze statistics and mathematical formulas related to programming•
Develop and validate solutions for complex problems using formal tests•
Debug logical errors in pseudo-code and flowcharts.•
Validate flowcharts and pseudo-code using desk checks•

Analyze solutions for progressively complex logical problems•
Evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of problem-solving approaches•
Develop and assess proofs of proposed solutions•
Create pseudo-code using standard algorithms and validate business requirements•
Debug errors in pseudo-code•
Analyze real-world case studies to contextualize logical constructs and problem-solving•

COURSE OUTLINE2025/2026
COURSE NAME: Front End Development Fundamentals
COURSE CODE: SDEV1150
COURSE DESCRIPTION
Almost all modern web applications rely on JavaScript for building great User Interfaces (UI) and User Experiences (UX).
Students will learn the fundamentals of JavaScript, how to handle client-side events, how to handle dynamic content, and how to
interact with backend applications. Additional topics taught will include how to use JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), the
Document Object Model (DOM), Modules, and package managers.
Course Credits: 3.00
Equivalent Courses: CPSC1520,WEBD2006
LEARNING OUTCOMES
OUTCOME Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to
1 Apply and adapt the JavaScript language to create and modify data structures, interact with external
data sources, and manipulate Document Object Model (DOM) content all within a client-side
environment.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Explain JavaScript data types (numbers, boolean, strings, arrays, objects) and their manipulation
methods
•
Demonstrate how to use JavaScript functions and variables to control the flow of a program•

Debug JavaScript code to identify and resolve errors related to DOM manipulation and data

COURSE OUTLINE2025/2026
COURSE NAME: Database Fundamentals
COURSE CODE: SDEV1201
COURSE DESCRIPTION
Databases and data are at the core of all businesses. This course will comprehensively cover how to design, build, and manage
relational database systems. Students will learn how to create, update, and delete data. They will also learn how to select data
using methods such as sorting, grouping, and filtering. Advanced topics will cover procedures, constraints, triggers, and
transactions in databases.
Course Credits: 3.00
Equivalent Courses: DMIT1508
LEARNING OUTCOMES
OUTCOME Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to
1 Analyze an organization’s data/business rules and design third normal form (3NF) entities utilizing the
normalization process and industry best practices to reduce data anomalies and create an efficient,
consistent, and effective entity-relationship model.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Understand the impact of data anomalies and redundancy in a relational database•
Use the normalization process to design a relational database in third normal form•
chunks.label: Page 1

chunks.text:
Understand the impact of data anomalies and redundancy in a relational database•
Use the normalization process to design a relational database in third normal form•
Create and interpret Entity Relationship Diagrams including cardinality and optionality symbols•
Discuss various relational database management systems and their use cases•
2 Write Structured Query Language (SQL) commands to create and alter tables, and add to, modify, and
remove data in a relational database.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Learn the DDL (Data Definition Language) syntax for creating and altering tables in a relational
database, including primary key, foreign key, check, default, and unique constraints
•
Use the DML (Data Manipulation Language) syntax to add, modify, and remove data•
Incorporate best practices and use style guides when developing SQL•
Discuss different database technologies•

3 Create accurate and maintainable SQL queries to retrieve data from a relational database to satisfy
users’ information needs utilizing one or more tables and various functions.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Use SQL SELECT statements to query a database including sorting, filtering, and aggregating•
Utilize debugging and testing strategies to check accuracy of queries•
Describe the different types of JOINs•
Use functions in SQL•
4 Construct stored procedures including transactions and error handling within a relational database to
improve security, performance, and code reusability.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Use decision structures•
Implement error handling in stored procedures•
Discuss debugging and testing strategies to verify logic•
5 Discuss database triggers and how they automate actions and enforce complex business rules within a
relational database.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Discuss use cases for trigger•
Discuss how triggers enforce business rules•

COURSE OUTLINE2025/2026
COURSE NAME: UI/UX for Developers
COURSE CODE: SDEV1701
COURSE DESCRIPTION
Students in this course will learn a foundation in User Interface (UI) design while covering the essential concepts of HTML
(HyperText Markup Language) and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets). Topics explored will include core design principles, semantic
structure, layout design, and other visual aspects for digital applications.
Course Credits: 3.00
LEARNING OUTCOMES
OUTCOME Upon successful completion of this course, you will be able to
1 Write well-structured HTML and apply and use CSS for the web.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Use HTML to design static web pages•
Explain why content is marked up with the specific HTML•
Apply fundamental CSS to HTML•
Design web pages using different CSS layout models•
Describe the CSS that was applied and the reasoning behind its application•
2 Create low fidelity wireframes to organize and structure information logically in a web application.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Apply HTML and CSS to design wireframes•
chunks.label: Page 1

chunks.text:
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Apply HTML and CSS to design wireframes•
Use modern design patterns to build attractive and familiar web pages•
Explain the decisions behind design choices•
3 Utilize fundamental design principles to create inclusive and accessible user friendly applications.
The following concepts, skills, and issues are used to support this Outcome:
Explain the user flows behind design choices•
Create flow diagrams to show different user flows on a website•
Design modern web layouts•

Style websites using modern styling frameworks•
Design reusable components that can be used in multiple places on a website•
